Marathon Petroleum climbed 0.4% today to $414.65, marking the fifth consecutive day of gains after a sharp 6.8% drop over the prior week. The rally appears tied to heating oil demand—prices for heating oil are up 59% year-over-year heading into winter, which typically boosts margins for refiners who produce it. Refineries are running at a healthy 95.2% capacity, positioned to capture this seasonal demand strength.

However, the broader oil market backdrop is mixed. Russian crude production has rebounded to 8.73 million barrels per day as global supply now exceeds demand, which puts downward pressure on oil prices and refiner margins. US crude is trading at $89.62 per barrel—lower than the $92.14 global benchmark—suggesting domestic supply is relatively ample despite the heating oil spike.
